items.title: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
items.summary: Talks in Abu Dhabi centred around Europe's security framework, with US envoys due to meet Putin and Zelensky on Thursday.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
items.summaryTr: Talks in Abu Dhabi centred around Europe's security framework, with US envoys due to meet Putin and Zelensky on Thursday.
items.articleText: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough - Published Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day. Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion. However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon. Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest." "I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible. Comments by Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky were less conciliatory. "Right now... a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the US, and on whether Europe comes to its senses," he said. After the talks it was announced that on Thursday US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - President Donald Trump's son-in-law - would travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to speak to Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky. The meetings in Abu Dhabi had been framed as centred around the "security architecture" of Europe. For Kyiv, this may include reassurances that allies will come to its aid if Ukraine comes under attack again, despite the country not being a Nato member. For Moscow, a reworked "security framework" is likely to include a limit to the influence of Nato in eastern Europe - a central concern for the Kremlin since the alliance's eastward expansion. Earlier this week Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while the Kremlin's Medinsky said the world needed a "new" and "fair" security system. That framework would serve as "a new Yalta and Potsdam", Medinsky said, referring to the 1940s summits in which the victorious Allied powers carved up post-war Europe into spheres of influence. Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin. Representatives of Britain, Nato and various EU countries were also in Abu Dhabi and met with US and Ukrainian negotiators, but the Kremlin - with whom the EU does not officially communicate - said its delegation had not had any contact with them. Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent. Many - particularly in eastern Europe - feel their security is linked to that of Ukraine. Agreements cannot be implemented "if no consensus can be reached among Nato members," a German government spokesperson said on Wednesday. Kushner said the US was keen to bring the Europeans on board and said that getting them "added to the format" would be on the agenda for his talks with Putin. There is also disagreement on whether discussions on a future security framework should be preceded by a ceasefire, as the Europeans and Kyiv would want, or whether the fighting only stops after an agreement has been reached, as the Kremlin has insisted. Any agreement on a peacetime security framework, however, is contingent on the war ending, Kushner noted. But that cannot occur "until there's an agreement on territory and on all other bilateral issues," he added. Since talks began last year, a core obstacle to any settlement has been Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are essential to its security. Moscow, meanwhile, has never backed down from its demand that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds. "Every inch" of land would be "returned to Russia one way or another", Medinsky said. Kushner acknowledged that the territorial question remained the hardest, while Zelensky's chief of staff and negotiator Kyrylo Budanov refused to be drawn on whether Russia was still demanding a Ukrainian withdrawal from the region. Later, Budanov admitted the talks had been "tough" and that Ukraine's priority was to ensure Russia could not attack it again. "These deals are very hard and complex, and this one is very emotional, very complex," Kushner said. "The reality is there is no trust right now between the sides and that is to be expected after a conflict like this." Related topics - Published1 day ago - Published21 hours ago
items.articleTextTr: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough - Published Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day. Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion. However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon. Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest." "I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible. Comments by Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky were less conciliatory. "Right now... a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the US, and on whether Europe comes to its senses," he said. After the talks it was announced that on Thursday US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - President Donald Trump's son-in-law - would travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to speak to Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky. The meetings in Abu Dhabi had been framed as centred around the "security architecture" of Europe. For Kyiv, this may include reassurances that allies will come to its aid if Ukraine comes under attack again, despite the country not being a Nato member. For Moscow, a reworked "security framework" is likely to include a limit to the influence of Nato in eastern Europe - a central concern for the Kremlin since the alliance's eastward expansion. Earlier this week Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while the Kremlin's Medinsky said the world needed a "new" and "fair" security system. That framework would serve as "a new Yalta and Potsdam", Medinsky said, referring to the 1940s summits in which the victorious Allied powers carved up post-war Europe into spheres of influence. Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin. Representatives of Britain, Nato and various EU countries were also in Abu Dhabi and met with US and Ukrainian negotiators, but the Kremlin - with whom the EU does not officially communicate - said its delegation had not had any contact with them. Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent. Many - particularly in eastern Europe - feel their security is linked to that of Ukraine. Agreements cannot be implemented "if no consensus can be reached among Nato members," a German government spokesperson said on Wednesday. Kushner said the US was keen to bring the Europeans on board and said that getting them "added to the format" would be on the agenda for his talks with Putin. There is also disagreement on whether discussions on a future security framework should be preceded by a ceasefire, as the Europeans and Kyiv would want, or whether the fighting only stops after an agreement has been reached, as the Kremlin has insisted. Any agreement on a peacetime security framework, however, is contingent on the war ending, Kushner noted. But that cannot occur "until there's an agreement on territory and on all other bilateral issues," he added. Since talks began last year, a core obstacle to any settlement has been Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are essential to its security. Moscow, meanwhile, has never backed down from its demand that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds. "Every inch" of land would be "returned to Russia one way or another", Medinsky said. Kushner acknowledged that the territorial question remained the hardest, while Zelensky's chief of staff and negotiator Kyrylo Budanov refused to be drawn on whether Russia was still demanding a Ukrainian withdrawal from the region. Later, Budanov admitted the talks had been "tough" and that Ukraine's priority was to ensure Russia could not attack it again. "These deals are very hard and complex, and this one is very emotional, very complex," Kushner said. "The reality is there is no trust right now between the sides and that is to be expected after a conflict like this." Related topics - Published1 day ago - Published21 hours ago

items.titleTr: Spain sees widespread disruption in first general strike for 14 years
items.summaryTr: Protests are also expected in the biggest cities less than three weeks before Spaniards vote in parliamentary elections.
items.articleText: Spain sees widespread disruption in first general strike for 14 years - Published Transport and other public services across Spain have faced serious disruption in the first general strike for 14 years called by the main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Demonstrations have taken place across the country, including in Madrid and Barcelona, where tens of thousands marched in the evening. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." However, the Spanish Confederation of Business Organisations said participation was "low and uneven", depending on the areas and sectors involved. Some of the biggest disruption on Wednesday was seen in the main industrial hubs of Madrid and the north-eastern region of Catalonia where traffic was halted on several main roads. The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices. The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later. Rental prices in the capital have soared in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50m sq apartment in Madrid was an average of €1,170 in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain's average gross monthly salary is about €2,460 (£2,056). That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions. Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform. Not since 2012, under the conservative government of Mariano Rajoy, has Spain held general strikes. And while previous strikes have been problematic for the government in power, this one is different. Sánchez and his ministers have even encouraged workers to down tools and demand affordable housing. "Your eight-hour day. Your pension. Your public healthcare… These were collective conquests," he wrote on social media, praising those who took part in previous strikes. Read more - Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage - Published23 September - Spanish PM Sánchez calls early election after housing protests - Published5 October The conservative People's Party (PP), by contrast, has accused the government of attempting to weaponise the strike for electoral gain. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called the general strike "nonsense", calling the unions "mafia" and "trash". Feijoo's party is leading in the polls and party spokesman Miguel Tellado accused the government of exploiting the strike to warn voters against allowing a right-wing government to be formed, which looks the most likely outcome of the 29 November election. Sánchez told Spanish TV this week: "What is nonsense is to question the rights of workers to strike." Among those taking part in the general strike was Gonzalo Álvarez, 27, who was visiting different picket lines in central Madrid. Although he works in sales, he has been volunteering for a housing union that tries to protect tenants and makes them aware of their rights. The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at the end of September "was the little fire" that sparked this protest, he told the BBC. Álvarez knew the 87-year-old, who had faced a tripling of her rent under new landlords, and says he was deeply upset by her treatment. He rents a small, one-bedroom flat with his girlfriend, a dental hygienist, in the city's southern Arganzuela disrict. The couple pay €1,000 between them, which means each spends about half of their salary on housing, even before other bills. "It's absolutely crazy… with the food, with the electricity, with the water, with gas." He sees no way of getting on the property ladder: "You have to collect an insane amount of money to be able to buy a house. So with these salaries, it's impossible." With current rent and purchase prices, he believes buying somewhere is "completely impossible". However, the vice-president of the CEOE, Spanish biggest business association, Miguel Garrido, criticised the strike, complaining that businesses had little to do with the price of housing. "This is not a strike for labour-related reasons, but rather for political ones, and it is closely linked to the early calling of elections," he said. Demonstrations were planned for some of Spain's biggest cities later in the day and the scale of support will be widely viewed as an indicator of public discontent ahead of the election. Another reliable indicator of support for strikes is the level of demand for electricity with Spain's industrial sector. Power usage in Spain fell by 7.5% during the early hours of Wednesday, according to data from operator Red Eléctrica. During the last general strike 14 years ago, equivalent consumption was down by more than 15%.

items.articleText: Satın alma onaylandı: Dev havayolu şirketi resmen satılıyor! Artık borsada olmayacaklar - EasyJet hissedarları, ABD'li Apollo'nun 5,7 milyar sterlinlik satın alma teklifini onayladı. AB incelemesinin ardından işlemin 2027'nin ilk çeyreği bitmeden tamamlanması hedefleniyor. Satış gerçekleşirse easyJet Londra Borsası'ndan ayrılacak. ABD merkezli özel sermaye şirketi Apollo'nun, İngiliz düşük maliyetli hava yolu easyJet'i 5,7 milyar sterlin karşılığında satın alma teklifi hissedarlar tarafından onaylandı. İşlemin gelecek yılın ilk çeyreği sona ermeden tamamlanması hedefleniyor. Hissedarların yüzde 97'sinden fazlası destekledi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle EasyJet'in açıklamasına göre, oylamada temsil edilen hisselerin yüzde 97,07'si satın alma anlaşması lehine oy kullandı. Oy hakkına sahip hissedarların yüzde 83,29'u da teklifi destekledi. Böylece şirketin özel mülkiyete geçerek borsadan ayrılması için gereken hissedar onayı eşiği aşılmış oldu. AB incelemesi bekleniyor Hissedar onayının ardından satın alma işlemi, Avrupa Birliği'nin düzenleyici kuralları kapsamında incelemeye alınacak. EasyJet, işlemin gelecek yılın ilk çeyreği sona ermeden tamamlanmasını hedefliyor. Satışın tamamlanması halinde easyJet, 25 yılı aşkın süredir işlem gördüğü Londra Borsası'ndan ayrılacak. İşlem, Avrupa'da bir hava yolu şirketine yönelik en büyük özel sermaye satın almalarından biri olmaya hazırlanıyor.

items.articleText: Borsa İstanbul’da 6 şirketten KAP açıklaması: Milyarlık anlaşmalar ve yeni yatırımlar Borsa İstanbul'da 6 şirket yeni iş ve yatırım gelişmelerini duyurdu. Hareket Proje'nin 4,5 milyon dolarlık anlaşmaları, Orge Enerji'nin 276 milyon TL'lik sözleşmesi ve Türkiye Kalkınma Bankası'nın 250 milyon euroluk kredisi öne çıktı. Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören 6 şirket, 11 Kasım Çarşamba günü yeni sözleşme, iş ilişkisi, yatırım ve finansman gelişmelerini Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) bildirdi. Açıklamalarda milyonlarca dolarlık anlaşmalar, jeotermal enerji yatırımı ve 250 milyon avroluk kredi öne çıktı. Hareket Proje (HRKET): 4,5 milyon dolarlık iki ayrı anlaşma Hareket Proje Taşımacılığı ve Yük Mühendisliği, Kazakistan ve Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri'ndeki projeler kapsamında ağır nakliye ve vinç kiralama hizmetleri için 2,5 milyon dolarlık anlaşma imzaladı. Şirket ayrıca vagon taşımacılığı ve proje kargo taşımacılığı hizmetleri için iki ayrı sözleşme yaptı. Üç ay sürmesi planlanan bu projelerin toplam bedeli 2 milyon dolar olarak açıklandı. DCT Trading (DCTTR): 34,8 milyon TL'lik pamuk alım anlaşması DCT Trading, 2026-2027 sezonu yurt içi pamuk alımları kapsamında 34 milyon 775 bin TL tutarında anlaşma imzaladı. Etap projesinde, Güzelbahçe Defne Evleri kapsamında 295 konut ve 20 ticari üniteden oluşan toplam 315 bağımsız bölüm için yapı ruhsatları alındı. Orge Enerji (ORGE): 276 milyon TL'lik veri merkezi sözleşmesi imzalandı Orge Enerji, Ankara'da inşası devam eden Veri Merkezi Projesi'nin ilk etap elektrik işlerine ilişkin sözleşme sürecini tamamladı. Şirketin 4 milyon 950 bin euro + KDV tutarındaki teklifi için işverenle sözleşme imzalandı. 23 Eylül 2026 tarihli TCMB kuru üzerinden yaklaşık 275 milyon 974 bin TL + KDV değerindeki işin 10 ayda tamamlanması planlanıyor. Kocaer Çelik (KCAER): İtalya merkezli şirketle jeotermal santral anlaşması Kocaer Çelik'in yüzde 99 iştiraki Kocaer Enerji, İtalya merkezli Exergy International ve Türkiye iştiraki Exergy Turkey ile santral tedarik sözleşmesi imzaladı. Sözleşme, Aydın'ın Buharkent ve Kuyucak ilçelerinde geliştirilen Kocaer-1 Jeotermal Enerji Santrali'nin ilk fazını kapsıyor. 12,34 MWe brüt kurulu güce sahip santral için ORC teknolojisine dayalı ekipmanların tasarımı, mühendisliği, imalatı ve tedariki gerçekleştirilecek. Türkiye Kalkınma ve Yatırım Bankası (KLNMA): KfW ile 250 milyon euroluk kredi Türkiye Kalkınma ve Yatırım Bankası, Alman Kalkınma Bankası KfW ile 250 milyon euro tutarında kredi anlaşması imzaladı.

items.articleText: Borsa İstanbul'da bir şirket TERA Fondaki hisselerini TMSF’den aldı - Blume Metal, tasfiye sürecindeki Tera Fon'da bulunan 497 bin 693 lot kendi hissesini TMSF'den pay başına 29,40 TL'ye satın aldı. İşlem sonrası şirketin elindeki payların sermayeye oranı yüzde 1,73'e yükseldi. Blume Metal Kimya A.Ş. (BLUME), Tasfiye sürecindeki Tera Fon'da bulunan 497 bin 693 adet kendi payını Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu'ndan (TMSF) satın aldı. İşlem, pay başına 29,40 TL kapanış fiyatı üzerinden gerçekleştirildi. 497 bin 693 lotluk hisse alımı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) yapılan açıklamaya göre TMSF, tasfiye sürecindeki Tera Fon'da bulunan 497 bin 693 lot BLUME payının öncelikle şirket tarafından satın alınmasını teklif etti. Blume Metal, yatırımcıları korumak ve ileriye dönük yatırım amacıyla söz konusu payları 11 Kasım 2026 tarihinde, 29,40 TL kapanış fiyatı üzerinden satın aldı. Şirketin elindeki payların oranı yüzde 1,73'e çıktı Açıklamada, işlemin pay geri alımı için ayrılan tutar dışındaki kaynaklardan karşılandığı belirtildi. Satın alma işleminin ardından Blume Metal'in sahip olduğu kendi paylarının nominal tutarı 3 milyon 33 bin 847 adede ulaştı. Bu payların şirket sermayesine oranı ise yüzde 1,73 olarak açıklandı.

Nvidia hisseleri, CEO Jensen Huang hakkındaki iddiaların şirketin faaliyetlerine olası etkileri tartışılırken iki günlük düşüşün ardından çarşamba günü yükseldi. Yatırımcılar, skandalın şirketin işlerine ve yapay zekâ yatırımlarına yansıyıp yansımayacağını değerlendiriyor. İki günlük düşüşün ardından yüzde 3,95 yükseldi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Nvidia hisseleri çarşamba günü yüzde 3 civarında yükselerek önceki iki işlem günündeki kayıpların ardından toparlandı. Hisse senedi pazartesi günü yüzde 4,3, salı günü ise yüzde 5,47 değer kaybetmişti. Düşüşte, Nvidia Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) Jensen Huang'ın Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılı olduğu öne sürülen bir kişiyle ilişkisine dair iddiaların şirkete olası etkileri belirleyici oldu. Nvidia, salı günü şirket sırlarının veya ulusal güvenliğin tehlikeye girip girmediğini araştırmak üzere Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz hukuk bürosuyla anlaştığını duyurdu. Yatırımcılar üç olası senaryoyu değerlendiriyor Bank of America, salı günü yayımladığı değerlendirmede gelişmelerin Nvidia üzerindeki etkisine ilişkin üç senaryoya dikkat çekti. İlk senaryoda krizin sınırlı kalması ve şirket yönetiminde devamlılığın korunması öngörülüyor. İkinci senaryoda ise belirsizliğin uzaması ve bilanço öncesinde şirketin değerlemesi üzerinde baskı oluşturması ihtimali bulunuyor. Üçüncü senaryoda soruşturmanın olumsuz sonuçlanması, yönetimde değişiklik yaşanması veya daha sıkı kısıtlamaların gündeme gelmesi halinde şirketin finansal görünümünün yeniden değerlendirilmesi gerekebileceği belirtiliyor. Zacks Baş Stratejisti John Blank ise satışların arkasında iki temel endişe bulunduğunu söyledi: ABD'nin gelişmelerin ardından yeni kısıtlamalar getirmesi ve iddialar hakkında yeni sorunların ortaya çıkması. Blank, CNBC'ye yaptığı değerlendirmede gelişmelerin Nvidia, Jensen Huang ve genel olarak yapay zekâ yatırımları açısından olumsuz olduğunu ifade etti. Morgan Stanley, Nvidia'yı en beğendiği hisseler listesinden çıkardı Morgan Stanley, çarşamba günü Nvidia'yı en beğendiği hisseler listesinden çıkardı. Bankanın bu kararı, Nvidia hisselerinin 2 Ekim'de listeye alınmasından bu yana yüzde 25'ten fazla değer kaybetmesinin ardından geldi. Analistler, Huang'ın liderliğinin Nvidia'nın stratejik yönü açısından kritik önem taşıdığını vurguladı. Şirketin üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 17 Kasım'da açıklaması bekleniyor. Huang'ın soruşturma sürerken ofise dönerek olağan iş akışını sürdürmeye çalıştığı, salı günü de toplantılarına devam ettiği bildirildi.
